components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 桌, 桥; 板 is a plank or board.
反 (fǎn) is a near sound match (-an); same part in 饭 fàn and 版 bǎn.

example.hanzi: 请把地板擦干净。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ dìbǎn cā gānjìng.
example.english: Please wipe the floor clean.
example.fact: 板 (from 木 "wood" plus the phonetic 反) means "a board, plank," so 地板 literally pictures a wooden floor laid over open ground; usage has since broadened well past wood alone to cover tile, laminate, and stone floors too, while 地面 stays the more general word for "ground" of any kind.

examples.hanzi: 地板上有一些水，小心别滑倒。
examples.pinyin: Dìbǎn shang yǒu yìxiē shuǐ, xiǎoxīn bié huá dǎo.
examples.english: There is some water on the floor, so be careful not to slip.

examples.hanzi: 我们家的地板是木头做的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā de dìbǎn shì mùtou zuò de.
examples.english: The floor of our house is made of wood.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 marks feelings, as in 想, 爱, 怒; 悲 is sorrow.
非 (fēi) — near sound — 悲 is bēi; 非 also sounds out 辈 bèi and 排 pái.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,她感到非常悲伤。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā gǎndào fēicháng bēishāng.
example.english: Hearing the news, she felt extremely sad.
example.fact: 悲伤 leans literary, common in writing or formal speech about grief and loss; in everyday conversation Mandarin speakers reach far more often for the plainer 难过 to describe the same feeling.

examples.hanzi: 他看起来很悲伤，一句话也不说。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlái hěn bēishāng, yí jù huà yě bù shuō.
examples.english: He looked sad and didn't say a word.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌的旋律让人感到悲伤。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē de xuánlǜ ràng rén gǎndào bēishāng.
examples.english: The melody of this song makes people feel sorrowful.

components.note: 小 (small) — 小 above 大 — a small top over a big base is a point.
口 (mouth) — calling and speech: 吗, 喊, 呼; 叫 is to shout.
丩 (jiū) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 纠 jiū.

example.hanzi: 看到蛇,她尖叫了一声。
example.pinyin: Kàndào shé, tā jiānjiào le yì shēng.
example.english: Seeing the snake, she let out a scream.
example.fact: 尖 ("sharp, pointed" — 小 "small" narrowing to a point above 大 "big" at the base) plus 叫 ("to call out") combine almost like a sound picture: a "sharp cry," about as literal as Chinese compounds get.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在游乐园里开心地尖叫。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài yóulèyuán lǐ kāixīn de jiānjiào.
examples.english: The children were shrieking happily at the amusement park.

examples.hanzi: 她被吓得尖叫起来。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi xià de jiānjiào qǐlái.
examples.english: She was so scared that she screamed.

components.note: 网 (net) — a picture of a hanging net with crossing cords; as a radical it appears as 罒 in 罚, 置, 罗.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 这些鞋子我是在网上买的。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē xiézi wǒ shì zài wǎngshàng mǎi de.
example.english: I bought these shoes online.
example.fact: 网 originally meant a woven fishing or hunting net (the character itself is a pictograph of mesh stretched on a frame); 网上 — literally "on the net" — is very likely a loan-translation of English "online," borrowed alongside "network" as computing terms entered Chinese in the 1980s–90s.

examples.hanzi: 我常常在网上看电影。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chángcháng zài wǎngshang kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: I often watch movies online.

examples.hanzi: 你可以在网上查一下火车时间。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài wǎngshang chá yíxià huǒchē shíjiān.
examples.english: You can check the train times online.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 说不定他已经知道这件事了。
example.pinyin: Shuōbudìng tā yǐjīng zhīdào zhè jiàn shì le.
example.english: Maybe he already knows about this.
example.fact: 说不定, built from 说 ("to say") plus 不定 ("not fixed, not certain"), sits at the more hedging, "I really can't be sure" end of Mandarin's maybe-words — a shade less confident than 可能 or 也许 — and it can open a sentence on its own the way "who knows, maybe..." does in English.

examples.hanzi: 明天说不定会下雨，带把伞吧。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān shuōbudìng huì xià yǔ, dài bǎ sǎn ba.
examples.english: It might rain tomorrow, so bring an umbrella.

examples.hanzi: 我也说不定，要看老板怎么安排。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yě shuōbudìng, yào kàn lǎobǎn zěnme ānpái.
examples.english: I can't say for sure; it depends on how the boss arranges things.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
二 (two) — the bottom bars. 丑 is an old calendar sign (the second branch) later borrowed for 'ugly'. Memory aid: a clown with two stripes, as in 小丑.
刀 (knife) — the dictionary lists a knife-like stroke group. The shape does not explain 'ugly'; Memory aid only.

example.hanzi: 马戏团里的小丑逗得孩子们哈哈大笑。
example.pinyin: Mǎxìtuán lǐ de xiǎochǒu dòu de háizimen hāhā dà xiào.
example.english: The clown in the circus made the children laugh out loud.
example.fact: 丑 has several unrelated senses — the 12th of the zodiac's earthly branches, and separately "ugly" — but the 丑 in 小丑 most likely traces to a third, older sense: one of the standard role-types in traditional Chinese opera, the comic character, from which "clown" generalized.

examples.hanzi: 小丑戴着红鼻子，表演得很有趣。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎochǒu dài zhe hóng bízi, biǎoyǎn de hěn yǒuqù.
examples.english: The clown wore a red nose and performed in a funny way.

examples.hanzi: 别把我当小丑，我是认真的。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ wǒ dāng xiǎochǒu, wǒ shì rènzhēn de.
examples.english: Don't treat me like a clown; I'm serious.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.

example.hanzi: 我喜欢看电视剧。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn diànshìjù.
example.english: I like watching TV series.
example.fact: 剧 means drama in 电视剧 (TV series), 京剧 (Peking opera), 话剧 (stage play) and 剧院 (theater). 追剧, 'to chase a series', is the everyday term for binge-watching. It can also mean intense: 剧烈.

examples.hanzi: 我周末去看了一场京剧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò qù kàn le yì chǎng jīngjù.
examples.english: I went to see a Peking opera on the weekend.

examples.hanzi: 这部喜剧很好笑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù xǐjù hěn hǎoxiào.
examples.english: This comedy is very funny.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.hanzi: 她正在读一本很有名的小说。
example.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài dú yì běn hěn yǒumíng de xiǎoshuō.
example.english: She's reading a very famous novel.
example.fact: 小说 literally reads "small talk" or "minor sayings"; in classical usage it originally referred to unofficial anecdotes and gossip beneath the notice of serious history-writing, and only narrowed over centuries to its modern sense, "novel, fiction."

examples.hanzi: 我很喜欢看侦探小说。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan kàn zhēntàn xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: I really like reading detective novels.

examples.hanzi: 这部小说已经被拍成了电影。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō yǐjīng bèi pāi chéng le diànyǐng.
examples.english: This novel has already been made into a movie.

components.note: 年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.
齿 (teeth) — 齿 is the tooth radical — age was read from teeth, as in 年龄.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 龄 is líng; 令 also sounds out 领 lǐng and 铃 líng.

example.hanzi: 请问,可以问一下您的年龄吗?
example.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, kěyǐ wèn yíxià nín de niánlíng ma?
example.english: Excuse me, may I ask your age?
example.fact: 龄's semantic component 齿 ("teeth") points to a real practice, estimating age by the condition of the teeth — still literally how a vet judges a horse's age today — and likely the origin of extending "tooth" to the abstract sense "age" in this character.

examples.hanzi: 你的年龄比我大还是小？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de niánlíng bǐ wǒ dà háishi xiǎo?
examples.english: Are you older or younger than me?

examples.hanzi: 不同年龄的人喜欢的音乐不一样。
examples.pinyin: Bù tóng niánlíng de rén xǐhuan de yīnyuè bù yíyàng.
examples.english: People of different ages like different kinds of music.

components.note: 交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 换 is to swap with the hands.
奂 (huàn) — same sound — 换 is huàn, like 奂; 奂 also sounds out 唤 huàn.

example.hanzi: 我们互相交换了电话号码。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen hùxiāng jiāohuàn le diànhuà hàomǎ.
example.english: We exchanged phone numbers with each other.
example.fact: 交换 wants a concrete, countable thing changing hands — gifts, seats, phone numbers — while its cousin 交流 is reserved for exchanging something intangible, like ideas or feelings; mixing the two up is a common learner slip.

examples.hanzi: 我想用旧手机交换一个新杯子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yòng jiù shǒujī jiāohuàn yí ge xīn bēizi.
examples.english: I'd like to swap my old phone for a new cup.

examples.hanzi: 你能和我交换一下座位吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng hé wǒ jiāohuàn yíxià zuòwèi ma?
examples.english: Could you switch seats with me?

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ⺮ is bamboo, as in 笔, 筷, 箱; tallies were bamboo slips split in two to match, so 符 is to match.
付 (fù) — near sound — 符 is fú; 付 also sounds out 附 fù and 府 fǔ.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.hanzi: 这份简历完全符合我们的要求。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn jiǎnlì wánquán fúhé wǒmen de yāoqiú.
example.english: This resume completely meets our requirements.
example.fact: 符 (⺮ "bamboo" plus the phonetic 付) refers to an ancient tally: a bamboo or wood token split in two, with each half's cut edge serving as a signature — the two halves "符合" (fit together) only if they were genuinely a matching pair, the root image behind today's sense "to accord with, to meet a requirement."

examples.hanzi: 这个办法符合我们的实际情况。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ fúhé wǒmen de shíjì qíngkuàng.
examples.english: This method fits our actual situation.

examples.hanzi: 这件产品不符合安全标准。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn chǎnpǐn bù fúhé ānquán biāozhǔn.
examples.english: This product does not meet the safety standards.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — weather radical, as in 雷 thunder, 雾 fog; snow is frozen rain.

example.hanzi: 北京冬天常常下雪。
example.pinyin: Běijīng dōngtiān chángcháng xià xuě.
example.english: It often snows in Beijing in winter.
example.fact: 'To snow' is 下雪, using 下 'to fall', just like 下雨. 小雪 and 大雪 are two of the 24 solar terms. The classical meaning 'to wipe away' lives on in 雪耻, to wipe away shame.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在院子里堆雪人。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài yuànzi li duī xuěrén.
examples.english: The kids are building a snowman in the yard.

examples.hanzi: 昨天夜里下了一场大雪。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān yèli xià le yì chǎng dàxuě.
examples.english: It snowed heavily last night.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions done by hand, as in 打 hit, 抱 hug, 拉 pull; fits 拥 to embrace or hold.
用 (yòng) is only a loose sound hint for yōng — same ending -ong.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打 hit, 拿 take, 把 hold; 抱 is to hug or hold in the arms.
包 (bāo) is a close sound clue for bào; it also sounds out 跑 pǎo, 饱 bǎo and 炮 pào.

example.hanzi: 他们在机场紧紧拥抱在一起。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài jīchǎng jǐnjǐn yōngbào zài yìqǐ.
example.english: They hugged each other tightly at the airport.
example.fact: 拥 and 抱 already each independently mean roughly "to hold in the arms" — 拥抱 doubles up two near-synonyms into one word, the same word-building strategy behind 喜欢 and 应该 elsewhere in this deck.

examples.hanzi: 朋友之间见面时，常常会拥抱一下。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou zhījiān jiànmiàn shí, chángcháng huì yōngbào yíxià.
examples.english: Friends often hug when they meet.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈给了我一个温暖的拥抱。
examples.pinyin: Māma gěi le wǒ yí ge wēnnuǎn de yōngbào.
examples.english: Mom gave me a warm hug.

components.note: 萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.

example.hanzi: 你带把伞吧,万一下雨呢。
example.pinyin: Nǐ dài bǎ sǎn ba, wànyī xiàyǔ ne.
example.english: Take an umbrella, just in case it rains.
example.fact: 万 ("ten thousand") plus 一 ("one") literally gives "one chance in ten thousand" — from that image of vanishingly low odds, 万一 became the word for hedging against an unlikely but undesirable possibility, typically opening a clause the way "in the unlikely event that..." does in English.

examples.hanzi: 万一我迟到了，你们先开始吧。
examples.pinyin: Wànyī wǒ chídào le, nǐmen xiān kāishǐ ba.
examples.english: If I happen to be late, you all go ahead and start.

examples.hanzi: 多存一点钱，以防万一。
examples.pinyin: Duō cún yìdiǎn qián, yǐ fáng wànyī.
examples.english: Save a bit more money just in case.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and spirits: 神, 礼, 福; 社 was an altar to the earth god 土.
土 (earth) — the earth god worshipped at the altar; hence a community that gathers there: society.
匸 (hiding box) — traditional 區 put several 品 (goods) in a box 匸: separate compartments, hence districts; 区 is area, in 地区.

example.hanzi: 我们社区新开了一家超市。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen shèqū xīn kāi le yì jiā chāoshì.
example.english: A new supermarket just opened in our community.
example.fact: 社 originally named the local earth-god a village worshipped together — its oldest sense is closer to "the community that shares a shrine" than to any modern institution; 社区's use for "community" in the sociological sense is comparatively recent, part of a wave of social-science vocabulary that entered Chinese in the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 我们社区有一个小图书馆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shèqū yǒu yí ge xiǎo túshūguǎn.
examples.english: Our neighborhood has a small library.

examples.hanzi: 社区里的邻居们经常一起锻炼。
examples.pinyin: Shèqū lǐ de línjūmen jīngcháng yìqǐ duànliàn.
examples.english: The neighbors in the community often exercise together.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 男, 努; 助 is to lend strength.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for zhù; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 姐 jiě.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 她是总经理的私人助理。
example.pinyin: Tā shì zǒngjīnglǐ de sīrén zhùlǐ.
example.english: She is the general manager's personal assistant.
example.fact: 助 (力 "strength" plus the phonetic 且) means "to lend one's strength, to help," and 理 (originally the natural grain running through jade, later "to manage, to put in order") combine fairly transparently into "one who helps manage" — a title, not just a helper.

examples.hanzi: 我是经理的助理，有事可以找我。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì jīnglǐ de zhùlǐ, yǒu shì kěyǐ zhǎo wǒ.
examples.english: I am the manager's assistant; you can come to me if you need anything.

examples.hanzi: 这位老师需要一个助理帮忙改作业。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎoshī xūyào yí ge zhùlǐ bāngmáng gǎi zuòyè.
examples.english: This teacher needs an assistant to help grade homework.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 谁发明了电话?
example.pinyin: Shéi fāmíng le diànhuà?
example.english: Who invented the telephone?
example.fact: 发明 always takes something that did not exist before — a device, a technique — which is exactly what separates it from the frequently confused 发现 ("to discover"), which uncovers something that was already there all along.

examples.hanzi: 这是谁发明的？真聪明。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì shéi fāmíng de? Zhēn cōngmíng.
examples.english: Who invented this? It's really clever.

examples.hanzi: 这个发明让我们的生活方便多了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fāmíng ràng wǒmen de shēnghuó fāngbiàn duō le.
examples.english: This invention has made our lives much more convenient.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 我正在跟客户通话,请稍等。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhèngzài gēn kèhù tōnghuà, qǐng shāo děng.
example.english: I'm on a call with a client right now, please hold on.
example.fact: 通 ("to pass through, to connect") plus 话 ("speech") gives "connected speech" — a fittingly literal way to name what a telephone call actually is, decades before "connection" became a tech buzzword in English too.

examples.hanzi: 我们通话了半个小时。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen tōnghuà le bàn ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: We talked on the phone for half an hour.

examples.hanzi: 这里信号不好，通话常常中断。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ xìnhào bù hǎo, tōnghuà chángcháng zhōngduàn.
examples.english: The signal is poor here, so calls are often cut off.

components.note: 交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.

example.hanzi: 下班时间,这条路的交通特别拥挤。
example.pinyin: Xiàbān shíjiān, zhè tiáo lù de jiāotōng tèbié yōngjǐ.
example.english: During rush hour, traffic on this road is especially congested.
example.fact: 交 (a person standing with legs crossed, "to intersect") plus 通 ("to pass through") build "crossing-through" — routes crisscrossing and passing each other — about as literal a picture of "traffic" as a two-character compound can offer.

examples.hanzi: 早上的交通比较拥挤。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang de jiāotōng bǐjiào yōngjǐ.
examples.english: Traffic is rather crowded in the morning.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市的公共交通很发达。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de gōnggòng jiāotōng hěn fādá.
examples.english: This city has a well-developed public transportation system.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — value and price, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy, 费 fee.

example.hanzi: 这件衣服太贵了。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài guì le.
example.english: This piece of clothing is too expensive.
example.fact: 贵 means costly, and also honored: 贵姓 asks 'your honorable surname', and 贵国 means 'your country'. It is also the abbreviation for Guizhou province (贵州). It is the opposite of 便宜 for price.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅贵不贵?
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng guì bu guì?
examples.english: Is this restaurant expensive?

examples.hanzi: 这个包比那个贵一百块。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bāo bǐ nàge guì yìbǎi kuài.
examples.english: This bag costs a hundred yuan more than that one.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.
口 (mouth) — mouth radical for speaking and sounds, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 唱 is to sing.
昌 (chāng) — same sound, different tone — 唱 is chàng; 昌 also sounds out 倡 chàng.

example.hanzi: 这位歌手将在体育馆演唱。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi gēshǒu jiāng zài tǐyùguǎn yǎnchàng.
example.english: This singer will perform at the stadium.
example.fact: 演唱 specifically implies singing as a performance for an audience — on a stage, at a concert — while bare 唱 covers singing in any context, including humming to yourself in the shower; the distinction survives in 演唱会, the everyday word for "concert."

examples.hanzi: 她在晚会上演唱了一首民歌。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǎnhuì shang yǎnchàng le yì shǒu míngē.
examples.english: She sang a folk song at the evening party.

examples.hanzi: 这个演唱会的票很难买。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yǎnchàng huì de piào hěn nán mǎi.
examples.english: Tickets for this concert are hard to get.

components.note: 重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 这是一项重大的决定。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí xiàng zhòngdà de juédìng.
example.english: This is a major decision.
example.fact: 重大 only modifies abstract nouns — events, decisions, discoveries, losses — never physical weight; for something literally heavy, Mandarin just uses 重 by itself, with 大 here contributing "magnitude" rather than "size."

examples.hanzi: 今天公司有一个重大的消息要宣布。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān gōngsī yǒu yí ge zhòngdà de xiāoxi yào xuānbù.
examples.english: The company has an important announcement to make today.

examples.hanzi: 这次事故造成了重大的损失。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shìgù zàochéng le zhòngdà de sǔnshī.
examples.english: This accident caused major losses.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; 组 is to weave threads together, so to form a group.
且 (qiě) loosely hints at zǔ; 组 sounds exactly like 祖 zǔ and 阻 zǔ, same part.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.hanzi: 这两种颜色组合在一起很好看。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng zhǒng yánsè zǔhé zài yìqǐ hěn hǎokàn.
example.english: These two colors look great combined together.
example.fact: 组合 is also the everyday word for a music group or idol group in Mandarin pop culture — a 男团/女团 "combination" of performers — an extension of the literal sense "to combine, combination" from mathematics and chemistry into entertainment.

examples.hanzi: 这几个词可以组合成一个新句子。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jǐ ge cí kěyǐ zǔhé chéng yí ge xīn jùzi.
examples.english: These words can be combined into a new sentence.

examples.hanzi: 他们是一个很受欢迎的歌唱组合。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì yí ge hěn shòu huānyíng de gēchàng zǔhé.
examples.english: They are a very popular singing group.

components.note: 田 here replaces 囟 (skull) in the older form: head over heart
心 (heart) — thinking and feeling, as in 想, 意, 感: 思 is to think over, with head and heart.
心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.hanzi: 这本书介绍了他的哲学思想。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū jièshào le tā de zhéxué sīxiǎng.
example.english: This book introduces his philosophical thought.
example.fact: 思想 carries real intellectual and even political weight in modern Chinese — it's the word in "毛泽东思想" (Mao Zedong Thought) — sitting well above the everyday 想法 ("idea, opinion") in formality, the way "philosophy" outranks "opinion" in English.

examples.hanzi: 他的思想很开放，愿意接受新事物。
examples.pinyin: Tā de sīxiǎng hěn kāifàng, yuànyì jiēshòu xīn shìwù.
examples.english: His thinking is open and he is willing to accept new things.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子很有自己的思想。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi hěn yǒu zìjǐ de sīxiǎng.
examples.english: This child has ideas of his own.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — mouth radical for speaking and sounds, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 唱 is to sing.
昌 (chāng) — same sound, different tone — 唱 is chàng; 昌 also sounds out 倡 chàng.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.hanzi: 这家店专门卖老唱片。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn zhuānmén mài lǎo chàngpiàn.
example.english: This shop specializes in selling old records.
example.fact: 片, a pictograph of a split log's cross-section — literally "a thin slice" — named the physical shellac and vinyl discs 唱片 once referred to; Mandarin has kept the same word for "album" even now that most 唱片 are digital files with no disc at all.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸收集了很多旧唱片。
examples.pinyin: Bàba shōují le hěn duō jiù chàngpiàn.
examples.english: Dad has collected many old records.

examples.hanzi: 她刚出了一张新唱片。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāng chū le yì zhāng xīn chàngpiàn.
examples.english: She just released a new album.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骗, 驾, 验; 骑 is to ride.
奇 (qí) — same sound — 骑 is qí, like 奇; 奇 also sounds out 椅 yǐ.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲的是中世纪骑士的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì zhōngshìjì qíshì de gùshi.
example.english: This movie tells the story of a medieval knight.
example.fact: 士 originally named a class of ancient Chinese warrior-scholars, the lower rung of the old aristocracy; 骑士 ("mounted 士") was coined by prefixing 骑 ("to ride") to translate the unrelated European idea of chivalric knighthood — the same word Chinese sportswriters also use for the NBA's Cleveland Cavaliers.

examples.hanzi: 骑士骑着白马，来到了城堡前。
examples.pinyin: Qíshì qí zhe bái mǎ, lái dào le chéngbǎo qián.
examples.english: The knight rode a white horse to the front of the castle.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢听骑士和龙的故事。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan tīng qíshì hé lóng de gùshi.
examples.english: Children like to hear stories about knights and dragons.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 洗 is to wash.
先 (xiān) — near sound — 洗 is xǐ; 先 also sounds out 选 xuǎn.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.

example.hanzi: 洗手间在走廊的尽头。
example.pinyin: Xǐshǒujiān zài zǒuláng de jìntóu.
example.english: The restroom is at the end of the hallway.
example.fact: 洗手间 literally means "hand-washing room" — a polite indirection for the toilet, functionally identical to English "restroom" or "washroom." The blunter, more clinical 厕所 names the same room but sits lower on the politeness scale.

examples.hanzi: 请问洗手间在哪儿？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn xǐshǒujiān zài nǎr?
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

examples.hanzi: 他去洗手间洗手了。
examples.pinyin: Tā qù xǐshǒujiān xǐ shǒu le.
examples.english: He went to the bathroom to wash his hands.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 哈 is the sound of laughing.
合 (hé) — near sound — 哈 is hā; 合 also sounds out 盒 hé.
口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 哈 is the sound of laughing.
合 (hé) — near sound — 哈 is hā; 合 also sounds out 盒 hé.

example.hanzi: “哈哈,你说得太对了!”他笑着说。
example.pinyin: “Hāhā, nǐ shuō de tài duì le!” tā xiàozhe shuō.
example.english: "Ha ha, you're so right!" he said, laughing.
example.fact: 哈哈 doubling or tripling in Chinese texting and chat (哈哈, 哈哈哈, 哈哈哈哈…) reads as genuinely warm, amused laughter, with more repetitions signaling more amusement — unlike English "ha ha," which can carry a flat or sarcastic edge depending on context.

examples.hanzi: 哈哈，这个笑话太好笑了！
examples.pinyin: Hāhā, zhège xiàohua tài hǎoxiào le!
examples.english: Haha, this joke is so funny!

examples.hanzi: 他看着我，哈哈大笑起来。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn zhe wǒ, hāhā dà xiào qǐlái.
examples.english: He looked at me and burst out laughing.

meanings: (Internet slang) previous poster in a forum thread

components.note: 木 (wood) — 木 is wood and trees, as in 树, 板, 桌; buildings with floors were built of wood, hence 楼.
娄 (lóu) — same sound — 楼 is lóu; 娄 also sounds out 搂 lǒu.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 楼上住着一对老夫妻。
example.pinyin: Lóushàng zhùzhe yí duì lǎo fūqī.
example.english: An elderly couple lives upstairs.
example.fact: Beyond its literal sense, forum culture reused 楼上 for "the poster right before me" — each reply in a thread is imagined as a floor (楼) stacked on the ones before it, so the previous post is, quite literally, "upstairs."

examples.hanzi: 我住三楼，他住在我楼上。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù sān lóu, tā zhù zài wǒ lóushàng.
examples.english: I live on the third floor, and he lives upstairs from me.

examples.hanzi: 楼上太吵了，我睡不着。
examples.pinyin: Lóushàng tài chǎo le, wǒ shuì bù zháo.
examples.english: It's too noisy upstairs and I can't sleep.

components.note: 车 (vehicle) — carrying loads by cart; also in 轮 wheel, 辆 for cars.
哉 (zāi) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 栽 zāi and 裁 cái. Note 载 reads zài in 下载.

example.hanzi: 这辆车可以载五个人。
example.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē kěyǐ zài wǔ gè rén.
example.english: This car can carry five people.
example.fact: 载 is read zài for 'carry' (装载, 载客) and in 下载 (to download). Read zǎi, it means 'to record' or 'year': 记载 (to record), 转载 (to repost), 三年五载 (several years).

examples.hanzi: 这辆卡车载着很多货物。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng kǎchē zài zhe hěn duō huòwù.
examples.english: This truck is carrying a lot of goods.

examples.hanzi: 请把软件下载到手机上。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ ruǎnjiàn xiàzài dào shǒujī shang.
examples.english: Please download the software onto your phone.

components.note: 圣 (holy) — traditional 聖 had an ear 耳 and a mouth 口: the sage who listens and speaks wisely.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech: 说, 话, 请; 诞 first meant big talk, then birth and birthday.
延 (yán) is only a loose sound hint for dàn.
耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 孩子们都相信圣诞老人会送礼物。
example.pinyin: Háizimen dōu xiāngxìn Shèngdàn Lǎorén huì sòng lǐwù.
example.english: Children all believe that Santa Claus will bring presents.
example.fact: 圣诞 literally means "holy birth" — Chinese's calque for "Christmas" as the nativity — and 老人 simply means "old person"; together 圣诞老人, "the holy-birth old man," is a transparent compound built to name a Western figure with no indigenous equivalent in Chinese folklore.

examples.hanzi: 圣诞老人骑着雪橇来送礼物。
examples.pinyin: Shèngdàn Lǎorén qí zhe xuěqiāo lái sòng lǐwù.
examples.english: Santa Claus comes riding a sleigh to deliver presents.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸在圣诞节那天扮成了圣诞老人。
examples.pinyin: Bàba zài Shèngdànjié nà tiān bàn chéng le Shèngdàn Lǎorén.
examples.english: Dad dressed up as Santa Claus on Christmas Day.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 逮 is to chase and catch. 隶 shows a hand grabbing a tail.

example.hanzi: 猫逮住了一只老鼠。
example.pinyin: Māo dǎizhù le yì zhī lǎoshǔ.
example.english: The cat caught a mouse.
example.fact: 逮 is read dǎi in the colloquial sense 'to catch' (逮鱼, 逮蚊子). In the formal word 逮捕 (to arrest) it is read dài. The colloquial reading is common in northern Mandarin.

examples.hanzi: 警察逮住了小偷。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá dǎi zhù le xiǎotōu.
examples.english: The police caught the thief.

examples.hanzi: 他想逮那只蝴蝶,可是没逮着。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng dǎi nà zhī húdié, kěshì méi dǎi zháo.
examples.english: He tried to catch that butterfly but couldn't.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁, 钟; mirrors were polished bronze.
竟 (jìng) — same sound — 镜 is jìng; 竟 also sounds out 境 jìng.

example.hanzi: 她在照镜子。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhào jìngzi.
example.english: She is looking in the mirror.
example.fact: 镜 builds many useful words: 镜子 (mirror), 眼镜 (glasses), 镜头 (camera lens), 望远镜 (telescope). A classical saying, 以史为镜, urges you to use history as a mirror.

examples.hanzi: 我的眼镜找不到了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yǎnjìng zhǎo bu dào le.
examples.english: I can't find my glasses.

examples.hanzi: 洗手间里有一面大镜子。
examples.pinyin: Xǐshǒujiān li yǒu yí miàn dà jìngzi.
examples.english: There is a big mirror in the restroom.

meanings: to be aimed at or against

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁; 针 is a metal needle.
十 (ten, cross) — 十 stands for the needle's shape, as in the old form 針.
寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.

example.hanzi: 这个广告是针对年轻人设计的。
example.pinyin: Zhège guǎnggào shì zhēnduì niánqīngrén shèjì de.
example.english: This advertisement is designed targeting young people.
example.fact: 针 ("needle," a fine point of metal) plus 对 ("facing, directed at") builds a fairly vivid image — "needle-pointed at" — for 针对's sense of being specifically aimed or directed at a particular target, whether a demographic, a problem, or a criticism.

examples.hanzi: 这些政策是针对环境问题制定的。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē zhèngcè shì zhēnduì huánjìng wèntí zhìdìng de.
examples.english: These policies were made to address environmental problems.

examples.hanzi: 他的话不是针对你。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà bú shì zhēnduì nǐ.
examples.english: His words weren't aimed at you.

meanings: one point (in a score or grade)
one fen (Chinese currency, 1/100 of a yuan)

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.hanzi: 他们的比赛只差一分。
example.pinyin: Tāmen de bǐsài zhǐ chà yì fēn.
example.english: Their game was decided by just one point.
example.fact: 分 alone already covers a small, fixed unit in several unrelated systems — a minute of time, a point of score, a fēn of currency (1/100 yuan) — so 一分 ("one 分") inherits whichever sense the surrounding context calls for, much like English "a point" shifts between sports, punctuation, and geometry.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试我只错了一分。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì wǒ zhǐ cuò le yì fēn.
examples.english: I lost only one point on this exam.

examples.hanzi: 等我一分钟，我马上就好。
examples.pinyin: Děng wǒ yì fēnzhōng, wǒ mǎshàng jiù hǎo.
examples.english: Wait a minute for me; I'll be ready right away.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 脸 face, 胖 plump, 脂 fat.
巴 (bā) is only a loose sound clue for féi.

example.hanzi: 这只猫太肥了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī māo tài féi le.
example.english: This cat is too fat.
example.fact: 肥 describes animals and meat (肥肉, fatty meat). For people, 胖 (pàng) is less harsh, and calling someone 肥 is rude. 肥 is also fertile or loose-fitting (肥沃, 肥大), and 减肥 is to go on a diet; 肥料 means fertilizer.

examples.hanzi: 这条裤子太肥了,我要换小一点的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi tài féi le, wǒ yào huàn xiǎo yìdiǎn de.
examples.english: These pants are too loose; I want a smaller pair.

examples.hanzi: 这片土地很肥沃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piàn tǔdì hěn féiwò.
examples.english: This land is very fertile.

components.note: 具 (tool) — two hands 廾 (the bottom 八) hold something valuable above — to provide, and a tool, as in 工具; 具 also sounds out 惧 jù.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).

example.hanzi: 请给我一个具体的例子。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí gè jùtǐ de lìzi.
example.english: Please give me a specific example.
example.fact: 具 (two hands, 八, holding up a tray, 目) already means "utensil, tool" — something with physical form you can hold — and 体 means "body, form"; together 具体 literally builds "having bodily form," the natural opposite of 抽象 ("abstract").

examples.hanzi: 你能说得更具体一点吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng shuō de gèng jùtǐ yìdiǎn ma?
examples.english: Could you be more specific?

examples.hanzi: 具体的时间还没有定下来。
examples.pinyin: Jùtǐ de shíjiān hái méiyǒu dìng xiàlái.
examples.english: The exact time hasn't been decided yet.

components.note: 片 (slice, plank) — marks flat pieces and wooden boards, as in 牌 sign; 版 is a printing block.
反 (fǎn) hints at the sound: 版 bǎn is close, as in 板 bǎn and 饭 fàn.

example.hanzi: 这本书有新版。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yǒu xīnbǎn.
example.english: This book has a new edition.
example.fact: 版 started as a printing block. It now covers editions and versions: 第二版 (second edition), 出版 (to publish), 版权 (copyright), 盗版 (pirated edition), 网页版 (web version).

examples.hanzi: 这本书的第二版出来了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de dì-èr bǎn chūlái le.
examples.english: The second edition of this book is out.

examples.hanzi: 你看今天报纸的头版了吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn jīntiān bàozhǐ de tóubǎn le ma?
examples.english: Did you see today's newspaper front page?

components.note: 页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 颜; 领 is the neck and then to lead.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 领 is lǐng; 令 also sounds out 龄 líng and 铃 líng.
寸 (hand, inch) — traditional 導 had 道 (road) plus 寸 (hand): a hand leading along a road; 道 dào is also a near-sound clue for 导 dǎo.

example.hanzi: 他是我们公司的领导。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de lǐngdǎo.
example.english: He is the leader of our company.
example.fact: In Chinese workplaces, 领导 doubles as a direct form of address — employees often call their boss 领导 to their face, the way one might say "boss" in English, rather than using a personal name or a specific title.

examples.hanzi: 我们的领导很关心员工。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de lǐngdǎo hěn guānxīn yuángōng.
examples.english: Our leader really cares about the employees.

examples.hanzi: 他领导着一个十个人的团队。
examples.pinyin: Tā lǐngdǎo zhe yí ge shí ge rén de tuánduì.
examples.english: He leads a team of ten people.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — two hands joined — 共 is doing together; it also sounds out 供 gōng.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.

example.hanzi: 大家要共同努力才能完成任务。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā yào gòngtóng nǔlì cái néng wánchéng rènwu.
example.english: Everyone needs to work together to complete the task.
example.fact: 共同 is almost always an adverb sitting right before a verb (共同努力, 共同决定, "work/decide together") rather than a free-standing word the way 一起 can be — you'd say 我们一起去, but 共同 needs a verb of shared effort to modify.

examples.hanzi: 我们有共同的爱好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu gòngtóng de àihào.
examples.english: We share a common hobby.

examples.hanzi: 两家公司共同投资了这个项目。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng jiā gōngsī gòngtóng tóuzī le zhège xiàngmù.
examples.english: The two companies jointly invested in this project.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 洗 is to wash.
先 (xiān) — near sound — 洗 is xǐ; 先 also sounds out 选 xuǎn.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 洗, 海; 澡 is bathing.
喿 (zào) — same sound — 澡 is zǎo; 喿 also sounds out 燥 zào and 操 cāo.

example.hanzi: 我每天早上洗澡。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang xǐzǎo.
example.english: I take a shower every morning.
example.fact: 洗澡 is a "verb + built-in object" compound — 澡 isn't a free-standing noun outside this word — so it can never take another direct object the way plain 洗 does in 洗衣服 ("wash clothes") or 洗碗 ("wash dishes"); "bathe" is baked into the verb itself.

examples.hanzi: 我习惯晚上洗澡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xíguàn wǎnshang xǐzǎo.
examples.english: I'm used to taking a bath at night.

examples.hanzi: 孩子正在洗澡，请稍等一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Háizi zhèngzài xǐzǎo, qǐng shāo děng yíhuìr.
examples.english: The child is taking a bath; please wait a moment.

components.note: 曲 (bent) — the shape pictures something bent; qū means crooked and qǔ means a song, as in 歌曲.

example.hanzi: 这首曲子很好听。
example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu qǔzi hěn hǎotīng.
example.english: This tune sounds lovely.
example.fact: 曲 is read qǔ for songs and music: 歌曲 (song), 作曲 (compose), 曲调 (melody). Read qū, it means bent: 弯曲 (to curve), 曲线 (curve), 曲折 (winding). Yuan-dynasty 曲 is a famous verse form.

examples.hanzi: 他会弹一首钢琴曲。
examples.pinyin: Tā huì tán yì shǒu gāngqín qǔ.
examples.english: He can play a piano piece.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌的作曲家是谁?
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē de zuòqǔjiā shì shéi?
examples.english: Who composed this song?

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁; 针 is a metal needle.
十 (ten, cross) — 十 stands for the needle's shape, as in the old form 針.

example.hanzi: 护士给我打了一针。
example.pinyin: Hùshi gěi wǒ dǎ le yì zhēn.
example.english: The nurse gave me an injection.
example.fact: 针 is a needle, and 打针 is to get an injection. It forms 针灸 (acupuncture) and 指南针 (compass), literally 'south-pointing needle'. 针 also counts shots and stitches.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶在用针缝衣服。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zài yòng zhēn féng yīfu.
examples.english: Grandma is sewing clothes with a needle.

examples.hanzi: 我最怕打针了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì pà dǎzhēn le.
examples.english: I'm most afraid of getting shots.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 稍 first meant the tip of the grain, a little bit.
肖 (xiāo) — near sound — 稍 is shāo; 肖 also sounds out 消 xiāo and 削 xiāo.
彳 (step) — the left part and radical, as in 往 and 行. It suggests going step by step; in 微 'tiny', as in 微笑 smile. Rest of the shape is unclear.
攵 (tap) — the bottom-right part, as in 收. Memory aid: tapping very lightly with tiny steps, so everything is 'slight'.

example.hanzi: 今天的天气比昨天稍微冷一点。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānqì bǐ zuótiān shāowēi lěng yìdiǎn.
example.english: Today's weather is slightly colder than yesterday.
example.fact: 稍微 rarely modifies a bare adjective by itself — it almost always teams up with a following 一点/一些/一下 (稍微冷一点, "slightly colder") to soften the degree, a pairing that trips up learners who drop the second half and leave the sentence feeling unfinished.

examples.hanzi: 请你稍微快一点，我们要迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ shāowēi kuài yìdiǎn, wǒmen yào chídào le.
examples.english: Please go a little faster; we're going to be late.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服稍微有点大。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu shāowēi yǒudiǎn dà.
examples.english: This piece of clothing is a little too big.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil and ground, as in 地 ground, 城 city wall, 坏 broken; 填 is filling a hole with earth.
真 (zhēn) — loose sound hint (tián vs zhēn); same part in 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn.

example.hanzi: 请填一下这张表。
example.pinyin: Qǐng tián yíxià zhè zhāng biǎo.
example.english: Please fill in this form.
example.fact: 填 is the verb for filling blanks on forms: 填表 (fill out a form), 填空 (fill in the blank), 填写 (complete). It also means filling a hole or gap, and 填饱肚子 means to fill your stomach.

examples.hanzi: 请在这里填你的名字。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèli tián nǐ de míngzi.
examples.english: Please fill in your name here.

examples.hanzi: 你填好申请表了吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ tián hǎo shēnqǐngbiǎo le ma?
examples.english: Have you filled out the application form?

components.note: 饣 (food) — 饣 is the simplified 食 (food), as in 饭, 饿, 饼; 饮 is a drink.
欠 (open mouth) — 欠 shows a person with an open mouth — taking a drink.
斗 (dipper, measure) — measuring grain and liquids: 科, 斜, 升; 料 is rice 米 measured out, then material.

example.hanzi: 你想喝点什么饮料?
example.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē diǎn shénme yǐnliào?
example.english: What would you like to drink?
example.fact: 饮 (饣 "food," narrowed here to drinking, plus the phonetic 欠) means "to drink," and 料, which elsewhere means "material, ingredient" (from an old image of measuring grain with a ladle, 斗), together give the literal "drinking material" — Mandarin's everyday word for "beverage."

examples.hanzi: 夏天我喜欢喝冰的饮料。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒ xǐhuan hē bīng de yǐnliào.
examples.english: In summer I like to drink cold beverages.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的饮料都很便宜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de yǐnliào dōu hěn piányi.
examples.english: The drinks in this shop are all cheap.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.

example.hanzi: 这条公路直接通向山顶。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo gōnglù zhíjiē tōngxiàng shāndǐng.
example.english: This highway leads directly to the mountaintop.
example.fact: 公 (八 "to divide" plus 厶, an old graph for "private") pictures private property being divided up to be shared fairly — the root of "public" — so 公路, "public road," names infrastructure by contrast with any privately owned lane or path.

examples.hanzi: 这条公路两边都是树。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo gōnglù liǎngbiān dōu shì shù.
examples.english: There are trees on both sides of this highway.

examples.hanzi: 我们开车沿着公路走了一整天。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kāi chē yánzhe gōnglù zǒu le yì zhěng tiān.
examples.english: We drove along the highway for a whole day.

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
页 (head, page) — heads and faces, as in 头 head, 顶 top, 额 forehead; 题 first meant forehead, then "heading".
是 (shì) gives a loose sound clue for tí; 是 also sounds out 提 tí and 堤 dī.

example.hanzi: 这次会议的主题是环境保护。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì huìyì de zhǔtí shì huánjìng bǎohù.
example.english: The theme of this meeting is environmental protection.
example.fact: 主 (originally a lamp's flame and stand, 丶 over 王, "the one who tends the light") narrowed to "main, master," and 题 (页 "head, forehead" plus the phonetic 是) named whatever sits at the top of a document — together, 主题 is close to literally "the main heading."

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章的主题是什么？
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng de zhǔtí shì shénme?
examples.english: What is the theme of this article?

examples.hanzi: 我们的婚礼以海洋为主题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de hūnlǐ yǐ hǎiyáng wéi zhǔtí.
examples.english: Our wedding has the ocean as its theme.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
皿 (dish) — 皿 is a vessel, as in 盘, 盒; 盗 is coveting what is not yours.
次 (drool) — 次 here originally pictured drooling — wanting something greedily.

example.hanzi: 这片海域曾经有海盗出没。
example.pinyin: Zhè piàn hǎiyù céngjīng yǒu hǎidào chūmò.
example.english: Pirates used to roam this stretch of sea.
example.fact: 盗 by itself means "to steal, a thief," and the same character resurfaces in 盗版 ("pirated edition") for bootlegged books, software, or films — Chinese independently extended "piracy" from sea-robbery to intellectual-property theft, the same metaphorical leap English made with the word "piracy."

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲的是一个海盗的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì yí ge hǎidào de gùshi.
examples.english: This movie tells the story of a pirate.

examples.hanzi: 海盗把宝藏埋在了小岛上。
examples.pinyin: Hǎidào bǎ bǎozàng mái zài le xiǎo dǎo shang.
examples.english: The pirates buried the treasure on a small island.

meanings: erhua variant of 一點|一点[yi1 dian3]

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: 麻烦你把音乐声音调小一点儿。
example.pinyin: Máfan nǐ bǎ yīnyuè shēngyīn tiáo xiǎo yìdiǎnr.
example.english: Could you please turn the music volume down a little?
example.fact: The 儿 in 一点儿 is erhua — a colloquial retroflex coloring of the final syllable rather than a separate spoken syllable, so despite being written with its own character, 一点儿 is pronounced as a single merged sound, yìdiǎnr, closer to Beijing-flavored speech than the equally correct, un-suffixed 一点.

examples.hanzi: 我只想吃一点儿，不太饿。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ xiǎng chī yìdiǎnr, bú tài è.
examples.english: I only want to eat a little; I'm not very hungry.

examples.hanzi: 今天比昨天冷一点儿。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: Today is a little colder than yesterday.
